source_corrections.evidence: the case assumes x is a boundary point and proves x belongs to both closures; the following sentence states the resulting containment for x
source_corrections.source_issue: the first case of the boundary-intersection proof concludes that the ambient space X is an element of the two closures rather than the point x
source_corrections.target_action: replace the membership subject X with x

source_corrections.evidence: the case assumes x is a boundary point and proves x belongs to both closures; the following sentence states the resulting containment for x
source_corrections.source_issue: the second case of the boundary-intersection proof concludes that the ambient space X is an element of the two closures rather than the point x
source_corrections.target_action: replace the membership subject X with x

source_corrections.evidence: the theorem hypothesis names b; its source exercise ex_CS_2 and the chapter summary both state the sequences converge to b
source_corrections.source_issue: the theorem introduces boundary point b but says the two constructed sequences converge to undefined x
source_corrections.target_action: replace the convergence target x with b

source_corrections.evidence: the repaired sequence lies in both A=(0,1) and B=[0,1] and retains the intended limit 0 with standard positive-integer indexing
source_corrections.source_issue: the sequence a_n=1/n indexed by every positive integer is claimed to lie in A=(0,1), but a_1=1 is not in A
source_corrections.target_action: use a_n=1/(n+1) for every positive integer n

source_corrections.evidence: the numerator sequence and positive-integer domain require the missing index n
source_corrections.source_issue: the set-builder expression for {1/n} omits its bound variable after the vertical bar
source_corrections.target_action: insert n before the membership relation n in Z+

source_corrections.evidence: every point of A is either a limit point or an isolated point in a metric space; hence A' union A^i equals A union A' and the next task states the needed containment
source_corrections.source_issue: the asserted identity A union A^i = A union A' is false in general because A^i is already contained in A
source_corrections.target_action: replace the left side with A' union A^i

source_corrections.evidence: the infimum on the right is over a in A of d(x,a), and the following statement uses the same point-to-set notation
source_corrections.source_issue: the prose defines the distance from x to A but the displayed left side is d(a,X)

source_corrections.evidence: the displayed identity is the arbitrary-family form of De Morgan's law, not de Moivre's formula
source_corrections.source_issue: the complement-of-intersection identity is attributed to DeMoivre's Theorem
source_corrections.target_action: identify it as De Morgan's law

source_corrections.evidence: the subject is an arbitrary union of open sets and the conclusion requires the copula
source_corrections.source_issue: the clause and so it an open set omits the verb is
source_corrections.target_action: translate the intended clause as and therefore it is an open set

source_corrections.evidence: the sentence introduces one function f from X to Y and the structural translation keeps the source mathematics intact
source_corrections.source_issue: the phrase Let f be a function f repeats the function symbol
source_corrections.target_action: recast the sentence as f is given and this function f maps X to Y while retaining both source math nodes

source_corrections.evidence: the phrase is as a subset of (R,d_E) and no equation occurs at that point
source_corrections.source_issue: the ambient metric-space expression is written =(R,d_E) with a spurious leading equals sign

source_corrections.evidence: thm_closed_sets_continuity_MS in the same chapter gives both directions
source_corrections.source_issue: the summary states only that closed preimages imply continuity although the chapter theorem proves an equivalence

source_corrections.evidence: both clauses have sequences as their grammatical subject
source_corrections.source_issue: plural sequences is paired with singular converges in two sentences

source_corrections.evidence: English auxiliary does requires the base verb tell
source_corrections.source_issue: the question What does the conclusion of part (b) tells us has an inflected verb after does
source_corrections.target_action: translate the intended question What does the conclusion of part (b) tell us

source_corrections.evidence: the paragraph and list are consecutive siblings; this is the same source pattern already repaired and schema-validated in the Chapter 9 summary
source_corrections.source_issue: the unordered list is nested inside a paragraph element and violates the pinned PreTeXt content model
source_corrections.target_action: close the introductory paragraph before the unordered list while preserving element order and prose

source_corrections.evidence: isolation forces all sufficiently late terms to equal a but imposes no restriction on a finite initial segment; the converse follows from the same eventual-constancy condition
source_corrections.source_issue: the prose can be read as claiming that the singular constant sequence (a) is the only sequence in A converging to isolated point a, although sequences with arbitrary finite prefixes also converge to a
source_corrections.target_action: state that every sequence in A converging to a is eventually constant with value a
